FR-O4: partly built: kernel/compile.py (init_repo, update_repo_surface) compiles each product's .gnomon/ (policy.toml, roles.toml, config.toml, system.md) from the routing as kernel commits on main, with the builder's write_allow equal to the contract tasks' write scope, every other role unable to write, and every cell's lane checking that surface out (FR-O4-AC-1, FR-O4-AC-2); not built: the write scope is one constant (WRITE_SCOPE: app/** and tests/**), not narrowed per envelope, because Gnomon has no per-run scope yet (upstream gap 1); the product policy.toml has no [governance.paths] list, so the contract and the surface are kept out of a cell's reach only by write_allow; and it has no [verify] block (contract preset, test_must_fail_first, protects, exit_on_fail, record_detail, finish gate) by design, since a verify command needs the owner's trust grant, so the kernel's gate runs those checks apart from the builder (kernel/lanes.py, kernel/gate.py)
FR-O5: partly built: kernel/gate.py judge traces each visible criterion at head (named by a test, the whole suite passing) and at base (the head's tests for each criterion copied onto the base revision, then onto the bare template, must fail) (FR-O5-AC-1, FR-O5-AC-2); not built: the kernel never runs `gnomon check --base <rev>` (no call in kernel/ or adapters/), so no change is judged by the base revision's Gnomon surface; and the head trace reads test names from the source and the suite's exit, not per-test reports, so a criterion whose only test is skipped passes the gate (found while testing, recorded as a bug, not fixed in this measuring wave)
FR-O7: partly built: kernel/change.py apply_change amends the spec and the contract only after a named person with a deciding persona accepts the change card in the Inbox, commits the new revision to the product's main, and reopens the tasks of the changed requirements; the gate keeps judging by the kernel's contract when a cell rewrites the product's copy (FR-O7-AC-1 to AC-3); not built: an amendment does not recompile the .gnomon/ surface (_recompile never calls update_repo_surface, and the surface does not derive from the contract); a defect's regression criterion enters the contract without a signed decision (by the triage table's design, FR-K2); a withdrawal cannot be applied (to_contract keeps a task for the withdrawn requirement, so the compile fails R-TRACE after the spec was already saved and approvals marked stale); task ids are positional, so adding a requirement to a project with a factory-default check hands that check's task id and state to the new requirement; and a builder cell's commit that edits contract.json or .gnomon/ merges into main when its gate passes (kernel/dispatch.py has no protected-path check, unlike kernel/workspace.py)
